item.title: Ukraine Barometer № 2: 2.3/5 · 17–23 November 2026
item.description:
Energy: strikes on substations continue, the south and east are going dark — Since September Russia has struck the energy system more than 1,000 times, mostly high-voltage substations (Energy Ministry). New outages hit 8 oblasts on 18 November and emergency cuts 5 oblasts on 22 November; Odesa's grid was damaged. NASA imagery shows national night brightness 9.5% below August, with Zaporizhzhia and Odesa oblasts darkest (about −30%).

About 60 paid-for Patriot missiles await Pentagon approval — According to the Financial Times, PAC-3 and PAC-2 interceptors funded by allies have still not been handed over because the US defence secretary has not signed off. The president reported talks with specific countries to speed up air-defence deliveries.

The EU formally tabled a €45bn loan for 2027 — On 18 November the Commission proposed a loan Ukraine repays only once it receives Russian reparations, with interest subsidised by EU states. Germany's chancellor threatened to veto the EU budget if all 27 do not back it. Leaders hold a first debate at the next summit.

Inflation confirmed: 11% in October — The statistics service confirmed annual inflation rose to 11% (10% in September), the highest since November 2024. The NBU's next rate decision is on 17 December; the hryvnia firmed slightly over the week.

The anti-corruption strategy again failed to reach a vote — As of 19 November bill No. 15230-d had not passed even a first reading, and the government is preparing its own version. In the Carthage case, investigators say SAPO has documented over UAH 1bn in illicit benefit and charged a former head of a Prosecutor General's Office department.

item.title: Ukraine Barometer № 1: 2.4/5 · 10–16 November 2026
item.description:
The power grid is in its worst state of the season — More than 310 attacks on energy facilities since the start of November. Scheduled outages in nearly every oblast, and all-day blackouts in parts of the country. Patriot interceptors arrive at about 12 a month, far too few to cover substations.

The economy has slipped from slow growth into contraction — Q3 GDP fell 0.7% year on year, inflation is rising and the NBU raised its key rate to 16.5%. The main drags are labour shortages and power outages.

2027 is short $32.6bn of external financing — The European Commission tables a €45bn loan on 18 November. Its fate depends on confidence in anti-corruption policy, which the Carthage case is now testing.

Talks resumed after a nine-month pause — Fourth trilateral round in Abu Dhabi. No breakthrough; Donbas is the core dispute. The achievable result is a prisoner exchange of 1,000–1,500 on each side.

Strikes on Russian refineries work, but only partly — Refining capacity is down about 30%, yet crude exports rose to 3.9m barrels a day and October revenue was 65% higher than a year earlier.
